title: NovaHealth — Security Posture & Deployment Options
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Discovery call focused on NovaHealth's security requirements for running patient-facing LLM features. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated or Private deployment because of PHI concerns and regulatory audit expectations. Main asks: provide SOC2 and ISO artifacts, explain SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC granularity, audit log retention options, KMS + HSM integration for key management, and confirm data retention / deletion guarantees. Next step: send SOC2 + whitepaper, draft RBAC matrix, and schedule a dedicated SE deep-dive with infra for network/VPC details.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-08 15:30 UTC | Duration approx 52m | Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (NovaHealth CISO), Ethan Moore (NovaHealth SRE), Anika Patel (Product), Carlos Vega (Infra), Maya Singh (Legal)
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Lena from Redwood — I'm the account lead — and with me is Marcus, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Rao: Hi Lena, thanks. Good. We're juggling some prep for the audit but excited to dig in.
[00:12] Marcus Chen: Great to meet you all. Quick agenda: run through your security posture needs, how Redwood's Hosted/Dedicated/Private fit, and then dig into specifics — SOC2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, retention. Sound OK?
[00:23] Ethan Moore: Yep. That's exactly it. We want to understand the risk surface before we commit to a pilot.
[00:28] Anika Patel: From product perspective, timeline is Q3 pilot but depends on security signoff.
[00:33] Lena Ortiz: Understood. Priya, can you start with a bit of context — what data types and regs are you most concerned about?
[00:40] Priya Rao: Sure. We're a healthcare platform, so there's PHI in some chat transcripts. We're in the US and EU, so HIPAA-ish expectations and GDPR for residency. We need to know whether customer data ever touches shared infrastructure or whether Dedicated / Private is the only acceptable path. Also SOC2 and ideally ISO 27001 evidence.
[00:58] Marcus Chen: Thanks. To be explicit: Hosted API runs on our multi-tenant platform; we offer data controls and can apply tenant isolation but for PHI and strict audit requirements many customers choose Dedicated or Private deployments. For Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools, isolated tenancy, and network-level options; Private gives you our control plane but fully VPC or on-prem where you manage the network.
[01:18] Carlos Vega: When you say Private on-prem — does Redwood ship an appliance, or is it container images we run?
[01:24] Marcus Chen: It's a package — Kubernetes manifests and operator for on-prem, and we provide an installer and optional air-gapped bundle. For VPC/private cloud we run a customer-dedicated control plane in your VPC or peered network.
[01:36] Priya Rao: Do you have customers running with PHI on Dedicated? Any references?
[01:41] Lena Ortiz: Yes — we've done several healthcare pilots on Dedicated and a handful on Private. We can share anonymized reference names + contact if you want.
[01:48] Maya Singh: We will need SOC2 Type II before procurement can move forward. Do you have a current report?
[01:54] Marcus Chen: Yes, we maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO certificate — we can share the SOC2 bridge letter and a redacted report under an NDA. I'll get that in the follow-up.
[02:04] Priya Rao: What's your data retention default on Hosted? And can we enforce deletion on Dedicated?
[02:10] Marcus Chen: On Hosted our default for logs and transcripts is 90 days unless configured otherwise; for Dedicated/Private, retention policies are customer-configurable and we support deletion-on-demand and data export. For PHI customers we usually recommend Dedicated with retention aligned to their policies.
[02:23] Ethan Moore: For auditability, we need immutable audit logs with at least 1 year retention and the ability to push logs to our SIEM. How do you do that?
[02:31] Marcus Chen: We provide a write-once audit stream for critical events and can forward logs to customer endpoints via syslog or direct S3 ingestion, and we support pushing to Splunk/Datadog. Retention is configurable; we also expose tamper-evident hashes in the log bundle.
[02:45] Anika Patel: How fine-grained is RBAC? Can we separate developer access from production model management and key usage?
[02:52] Marcus Chen: Yes. Our RBAC model supports role templates and custom roles. You can separate: API keys/clients, infra operators, model dev, and audit-only viewers. For Dedicated/Private we integrate with SSO via SAML and SCIM to sync groups and map to roles.
[03:06] Marcus Chen: Quick caveat — SAML SSO for Hosted is through our multi-tenant auth layer; for Private we'll integrate to your IdP directly.
[03:13] Priya Rao: Does your SSO support SCIM for automatic provisioning? We don't want to manage users manually.
[03:19] Marcus Chen: Yes, SCIM for user and group provisioning is supported for both Dedicated and Private, and for Hosted we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML flows.
[03:26] Carlos Vega: KMS — we need HSM-backed key custody and zero-access from the vendor. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[03:33] Marcus Chen: Absolutely. For Dedicated and Private we support customer KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) workflows. For the highest assurance, on Private on-prem we can integrate with an HSM and you hold the master key. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and a customer-managed key option in certain enterprise plans.
[03:52] Priya Rao: Important: legal will not accept vendor that can decrypt stored content without customer approval.
[03:58] Lena Ortiz: We have contractual clauses and technical controls to enforce that. We'll include key custody language in the security pack we send.
[04:05] Maya Singh: Audit logs — who has access to those logs? Are they readable by Redwood ops?
[04:10] Marcus Chen: By default, Redwood ops has limited access under break-glass procedures that are logged and require approval. For Dedicated/Private, logs can be shipped to your own SIEM so Redwood ops doesn't need access. We'll document the access model.
[04:21] Ethan Moore: Network wise, for Dedicated do we get private IPs and option to restrict egress? We need to ensure no outbound to the public internet from inference nodes.
[04:29] Marcus Chen: Yes, Dedicated uses VPC peering or private connectivity. You can lock down egress and control NAT gateways. For Private on-prem, of course everything stays on your network.
[04:37] Priya Rao: How about pen tests and vulnerability disclosure — do you publish a program?
[04:42] Marcus Chen: We have a coordinated disclosure policy and run regular internal pentests; for enterprise customers we can coordinate scope for third-party assessments and share remediation timelines.
[04:50] Anika Patel: A practical question: if we do a Dedicated pilot, can we start with a small reserved pool then scale up?
[04:56] Lena Ortiz: Yes. You can start with a reserved baseline and enable burst capacity. We'll include configuration recommendations based on workload.
[05:03] Priya Rao: On compliance, do you support processing agreements for HIPAA? BAAs?
[05:09] Marcus Chen: We do sign BAAs for customers who require HIPAA protections. The BAAs sit alongside the contract.
[05:15] Priya Rao: Great. For the SOC2 evidence — can you provide the last two years? We need to validate control changes.
[05:21] Marcus Chen: We can provide the latest SOC2 Type II report and a summary of any control changes. Older reports we can discuss, but usually we provide the latest and a bridge letter.
[05:30] Maya Singh: For legal review, we need sample contract language for encryption, data deletion SLA, and indemnity around data breaches.
[05:37] Lena Ortiz: We'll have legal share redlined examples and the standard enterprise addendum. I'll loop in our contracts lead.
[05:44] Carlos Vega: Does Redwood provide any tools for model explainability or data lineage? We need to trace which prompts produced which responses for auditability.
[05:51] Marcus Chen: We have request-level tracing with request IDs, prompt/hypothesis fingerprints and optional payload hashing; those feed into our audit logs. We also have token-level cost traces if you need that for billing.
[06:05] Priya Rao: About data residency — do you have EU regions for serving and storage?
[06:11] Marcus Chen: Yes, Redwood has EU and NA regions; Dedicated can be provisioned in-region. Private is under your control for residency.
[06:18] Anika Patel: If we wanted to do on-prem air-gapped, what's the install cadence and support model?
[06:24] Marcus Chen: Air-gapped installs are handled by our deployment team with a multi-week cadence depending on environment complexity. We provide an operator bundle and offline docs; support is on an enterprise SLA.
[06:33] Priya Rao: Regarding RBAC — does your audit log capture privilege elevation events?
[06:38] Marcus Chen: Yes, role changes, elevation, token creation, and key access are all first-class audit events. We can provide an event schema.
[06:45] Maya Singh: Can we require MFA for all admin actions?
[06:49] Marcus Chen: Yes — we support enforced MFA through your IdP for admin groups, and we also have device/session policies you can configure.
[06:56] Lena Ortiz: Quick note on encryption at rest: For Hosted we encrypt everything at rest using disk-level encryption and we use envelope encryption for secrets. For Dedicated and Private you can use your own KMS or HSM.
[07:08] Priya Rao: We need to confirm that Redwood cannot access unencrypted training or inference logs in Hosted mode.
[07:14] Marcus Chen: For Hosted, raw unencrypted artifacts are not accessible to Redwood engineers unless you opt-in or in break-glass scenarios; access is logged. For customers that require zero-access, Dedicated or Private is the recommended path.
[07:26] Ethan Moore: Operationally, if we do Dedicated, who handles patching of the runtime? And what's the windows for critical security patches?
[07:34] Marcus Chen: For Dedicated we manage the serving runtime and handle patching as part of the managed service; we do scheduled maintenance windows, and critical patches are pushed under emergency change controls. For Private on-prem, we provide patches and bundles and you can choose timing if you want to run the operator.
[07:49] Priya Rao: Can you show a sample RBAC matrix?
[07:52] Marcus Chen: Yes, I'll attach a sample roles & permissions matrix in the follow-up.
[07:57] Lena Ortiz: Sounds like we have action items — Maya/legal wants contract language around BAAs and deletion; Priya wants SOC2/ISO artifacts; Carlos wants network/VPC spec; Ethan wants log forwarding + retention policies; Marcus will schedule a technical deep-dive.
[08:10] Priya Rao: Also, can you confirm whether we can rotate keys without downtime? That's important for our key rotation policy.
[08:16] Marcus Chen: We support zero-downtime key rotation using envelope keys and active key switching; we'll document the procedure.
[08:24] Anika Patel: For data deletion, is there an audit trail showing who requested deletion and when?
[08:29] Marcus Chen: Yes, deletion requests produce an auditable event with a request ID and operator identity; we also provide the deletion manifest.
[08:36] Maya Singh: If a breach happened, what is your notification SLA?
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: We have an incident response playbook; standard notification windows are 72 hours for confirmed data breaches and immediate if there's PII/PHI exposure. We'll include the IR summary.
[08:52] Priya Rao: For the pilot, what level of data will be sent? We'll likely do pseudonymized payloads initially.
[08:59] Ethan Moore: Yes, we'll pseudonymize, but we also need to test with a sample of de-identified PHI to validate behavior.
[09:06] Marcus Chen: Understood — we can support a staged approach: synthetic/pseudonymized first, then limited PHI under BAA in Dedicated.
[09:12] Lena Ortiz: Ok, let's list concrete next steps. Marcus, can you confirm deliverables?
[09:18] Marcus Chen: Sure — I'll send: 1) SOC2 Type II redacted report + bridge letter (NDA if required), 2) ISO summary, 3) RBAC sample matrix, 4) KMS/HSM integration doc + key rotation steps, 5) network/VPC spec for Dedicated, 6) incident response summary, 7) sample contract clauses for data deletion and encryption, and 8) schedule for a 60-minute SE deep-dive for network and install specifics.
[09:48] Maya Singh: Can you also include the legal contact for contract redlines and the standard BAA template?
[09:52] Lena Ortiz: Yes, I'll include our contracts lead and legal contact.
[09:56] Priya Rao: Timeline — we need the security docs by 2025-05-15 for our risk review. Can that be met?
[10:02] Lena Ortiz: We'll aim to deliver by 2025-05-15; Marcus will own the SOC2 artifacts and the SE docs.
[10:08] Ethan Moore: For the SE deep-dive, we need a slot next week for a 1h block focusing on VPC peering, private DNS, and egress controls.
[10:15] Marcus Chen: I'll propose 3 slots and include a pre-call checklist so we can gather network diagrams and CIDR blocks.
[10:21] Anika Patel: Any blockers from Redwood's side to run a short benchmark in Dedicated? We want latency numbers with our 512-token prompts.
[10:27] Marcus Chen: No blockers — we can spin up a small Dedicated pool for benchmark and provide latency/cost profiles. We'll need your prompt set and expected concurrency.
[10:34] Priya Rao: One last question — do you support legal hold for deleted records? For litigation we might need to restore.
[10:40] Marcus Chen: We support configurable retention holds and export snapshots; we can discuss the legal hold workflow in the follow-up.
[10:48] Lena Ortiz: Great. Any other questions?
[10:51] Priya Rao: Not from me.
[10:52] Carlos Vega: Nothing else.
[10:53] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the security pack and the SE scheduling.
[10:58] (end)

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (e.g., "V-P-C" for "VPC"), some speaker overlaps, filler words present. References shared: Redwood security pack link (sent in follow-up), sample RBAC matrix (attached in follow-up), SOC2 report (redacted, via NDA).

Marcus to attach RBAC matrix and KMS integration doc
